slides.title: Variables and data types
slides.html:
Basics

Variables and data types

  • const for values that never change
  • let for values that will change
  • Avoid var (old and confusing)
  • Types: string, number, boolean, null, undefined
  • typeof tells you a value's type

variables.js

const name = "Ada";        // string
let score = 72;            // number
const isStudent = true;    // boolean
let nickname = null;       // empty on purpose
let city;                  // undefined
 
score = score + 5;         // let can change
console.log(typeof score); // "number"

slides.title: Operators and conditions
slides.html:
Basics

Operators and conditions

  • Maths: + - * / %
  • Compare with === and !==, never ==
  • Combine with && (and), || (or), ! (not)
  • switch is neat when one value has many cases

conditions.js

if (score >= 70) {
  console.log("Distinction");
} else if (score >= 50) {
  console.log("Pass");
} else {
  console.log("Try again");
}
 
switch (day) {
  case "Sat": console.log("Weekend!"); break;
  case "Mon": console.log("Class day"); break;
  default: console.log("Keep building");
}

slides.title: Loops: for and while
slides.html:
Basics

Loops: for and while

  • for when you know how many times
  • for…of to go through an array
  • while repeats until a condition is false
  • Watch out for loops that never stop

loops.js

for (let i = 1; i <= 3; i++) {
  console.log(`Lesson ${i}`);
}
 
const tracks = ["Frontend", "Backend"];
for (const track of tracks) {
  console.log(track);
}
 
let tries = 0;
while (tries < 3) {
  tries++;
}

slides.title: Functions and arrow functions
slides.html:
Reusable code

Functions and arrow functions

  • A function is reusable code with a name
  • It takes parameters and returns a value
  • Arrow functions are a shorter way to write them
  • One-line arrows return automatically

functions.js

function greet(name) {
  return `Hello, ${name}!`;
}
 
const add = (a, b) => a + b;
 
const welcome = (name = "student") =>
  `Welcome to BlockHub, ${name}`;
 
console.log(greet("Ada")); // Hello, Ada!
console.log(add(2, 3));    // 5

slides.title: Arrays and array methods
slides.html:
Working with data

Arrays and array methods

  • An array is an ordered list
  • map: change every item
  • filter: keep the items that pass a test
  • find: get the first match

arrays.js

const prices = [1500, 4000, 800, 2500];
 
const withVat = prices.map((p) => p * 1.075);
const cheap = prices.filter((p) => p < 2000);
const first = prices.find((p) => p > 3000);
 
console.log(cheap);       // [1500, 800]
console.log(first);       // 4000
console.log(prices.length); // 4

slides.title: Objects
slides.html:
Working with data

Objects

  • Objects group related data as key: value
  • Read with dot notation
  • Add or change keys any time
  • Arrays of objects are how real apps store data

objects.js

const student = {
  name: "Ada",
  track: "Full-Stack",
  scores: [72, 85],
};
 
console.log(student.name);  // "Ada"
student.city = "Lagos";     // add a key
student.track = "Frontend"; // change a key
 
const { name, city } = student; // destructuring

slides.html:
The DOM

Select and change elements

index.html

<h1 id="title">Hello</h1>
<p class="note">Old text</p>

slides.title: Events and event listeners
slides.html:
The DOM

Events and event listeners

  • An event is something the user does: click, type, submit
  • addEventListener runs your function when it happens
  • event.preventDefault() stops a form reloading the page

app.js

const btn = document.querySelector("#btn");
const count = document.querySelector("#count");
let clicks = 0;
 
btn.addEventListener("click", () => {
  clicks++;
  count.textContent = `Clicked ${clicks} times`;
});
 
form.addEventListener("submit", (event) => {
  event.preventDefault();
});

slides.title: Debugging with the console
slides.html:
Debugging

Debugging with the console

  • Open DevTools: F12, then Console
  • console.log shows values as your code runs
  • Red errors tell you the file and line
  • Read the error message first: it usually says what's wrong

debug.js

console.log("score is", score);
console.table(students);
console.error("Something failed");
 
// Common error:
// TypeError: Cannot read properties of null
// means querySelector found nothing.
// Check the id/class, and that the script
// loads after the HTML.

slides.title: Dark mode toggle
slides.html:
Build · step 1

Dark mode toggle

  • One class on body controls the theme
  • classList.toggle adds or removes it
  • CSS does the rest

<button id="theme">🌙 Dark mode</button>
 
// app.js
const themeBtn = document.querySelector("#theme");
 
themeBtn.addEventListener("click", () => {
  document.body.classList.toggle("dark");
  const dark = document.body.classList.contains("dark");
  themeBtn.textContent = dark ? "☀️ Light mode" : "🌙 Dark mode";
});

slides.title: To-do list
slides.html:
Build · step 2

To-do list

  • Read the input value
  • Create an element with createElement
  • Add it to the list with append
  • Clear the input for the next task

app.js

const form = document.querySelector("#todo-form");
const input = document.querySelector("#todo-input");
const list = document.querySelector("#todo-list");
 
form.addEventListener("submit", (event) => {
  event.preventDefault();
  if (!input.value.trim()) return;
  const li = document.createElement("li");
  li.textContent = input.value;
  li.addEventListener("click", () => li.remove());
  list.append(li);
  input.value = "";
});
